chunks: From Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim said: Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, he said: Hisham al-Mashriqi narrated to me,

He entered upon Abu al-Hasan al-Khurasani (peace be upon him) and said: The people of Basra inquired about Divine Speech, saying: Yunus says that Speech is not created. I said to them: Yunus has spoken the truth, Speech is not created. Has not reached you the statement of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when he was asked about the Qur'an: Is it a Creator or created? He said to them: It is neither a Creator nor created, rather it is the Speech of the Creator. Thus the position of Yunus was strengthened. And they said: Yunus says that it is from the Sunnah for a man to pray two units while seated after the night prayer (Isha). I said: Yunus has spoken the truth.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on whether the Quran/Divine Speech is created or uncreated?
ai.summary: This narration from Rijal al-Kashshi highlights the Ash'ari-leaning view of Yunus ibn Abi 'Imran, who affirmed that the Qur'an is the uncreated Speech of Allah, thereby avoiding the extremes of calling it 'created' (as per the Mu'tazila) or 'a created entity' (as per some others). The text also records a specific juristic practice attributed to Yunus: performing two voluntary rak'ahs while seated after the 'Isha prayer, reflecting the practical application of Imami jurisprudence during the era of the Four Deputies.

en.ammaar-muslim: [3/1575] Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim from Muhammad b. Isa from Hisham al-Mashriqi that he (i.e. Hisham) entered in to see Abi al-Hasan al-Khurasani (a.s.)

who said: The people of Basra inquired about Divine Speech and said ‘Yūnus says that Divine Speech is not created!’ I said to them: ’Yūnus has spoken the truth, Divine Speech is not created. Has the statement of Abī Jaʿfar (a.s.) not reached you when he was asked about the Qur’an ‘is it a creator or created?’ He said to them: ’It is neither a creator nor created, rather it is the Speech of the Creator.’  Thus I strengthened the position of Yūnus. They (i.e. the people of Basra) also said ‘Yūnus says that it is from the Sunnah for a man to pray two units while seated after the final night prayer (i.e. ʿIshāʾ)’. I said: Yūnus has spoken the truth.
